rv.q: Jane Fonda's return to Broadway after 46 years is the main draw of '33 Variations,' but the play itself is a thoughtful meditation on creativity and mortality that stands on its own merits.

Ms. Fonda’s layered crispness is, I regret to add, a contrast to Mr. Kaufman’s often soggy play, which sends her character on a quest to unlock, with a mortal deadline looming before her, a musical mystery about the Beethoven composition of the title.
"33 Variations" so busily tries to impress you with its civility and erudition that it neglects to make you care.
This does not make '33 Variations' a good play or suggest that the actress, 71, has bounced back onto the stage with all the easygoing confide
Fonda's seemingly congenital inability to suggest weakness undermines both her character and the play's dynamics.

Jane Fonda's return to Broadway after 46 years is reason enough to see 33 Variations, but fortunately Moisés Kaufman's play about obsession, legacy, and the creative process provides plenty of other compelling reasons as well.
Kaufman makes a convincing case for the genius of emotional variation in each of us, whether we're Beethoven or not.
Fonda fans, of whom I am one, will not be disappointed, though they may be surprised.
Their performances, along with some glorious music, make 33 Variations engaging in spite of its contrivances.
Too bad this handsomely designed but unconvincing drama isn't as big an event as Fonda's return.

cn.t: Fonda's triumphant Broadway return after 46 years anchors Kaufman's ambitious meditation on creativity and mortality. Critics praise her layered performance, though some find the play itself uneven despite its thoughtful themes and musical intelligence.

vs.sum: The Eugene O'Neill Theatre offers decent sightlines, though some seats may have minor obstructions due to the shallow rake. Sound quality is generally good, ensuring an enjoyable auditory experience. While the comfort level is typical for Broadway, with standard legroom and seat width, the theater's ambiance is enhanced by its elegant Georgian design. Facilities are adequate, with bars and merchandise available on both levels, though restroom capacity may be limited during peak times.

acc.note: No elevators. All accessible seating on Orchestra level. Infrared headsets and audio induction neck loops.
